what_happened: Research found the existing batch-orchestration-guardrails.md concurrency objection for a per-task postflight deploy trigger ('sibling task's own still-in-flight dispatch') does not hold at the same-cycle Move 2/Move 3 boundary by the same cycle-synchronicity argument the doc already uses for the Inter-Cycle Checkpoint; the real residual risk there is cross-session lock contention, already accepted at the two existing trigger sites. Recommendation is still no behavioral change, on cost/benefit (test-lint-deploy-caller-wrap.sh's two-caller invariant) rather than pure safety grounds.

Research delivered an explicit negative-but-documented verdict with a ready-to-adapt draft of the target subsection in its Appendix, so the plan phase needed no re-derivation of the safety/cost argument and could be scoped to a three-phase documentation-only change in one pass.

Planning surfaced a hazard research had not flagged: a pointer comment naming deploy-headless.sh could in principle be misclassified by the caller-wrap lint as a new genuine caller. Read the lint's classify_line function to confirm it short-circuits any line whose first non-whitespace char is '#' to MENTION, then recorded the constraint explicitly in the plan's risk table and Phase 2 verification rather than leaving it implicit.

Phase 1 gate 3 (doc-lint) failed on index-entries.json line_count drift for batch-orchestration-guardrails.md after inserting the new subsection; two other unrelated entries were already stale pre-dispatch. Remedy: bash .claude/scripts/generate-context-line-counts.sh --write (must run from the deployed tree, not the source store -- the source-store copy errors with a bogus-root message). The two pre-existing drifted entries were left for the containment self-check to exclude from this phase's commit since they are outside this task's file_scope.
